chunks: Ḥannān ibn Sadīr narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, that he said:
"O ʿAbd Allāh, there is no Eid for the Muslims, whether Eid al-Aḍḥā or Eid al-Fiṭr, except that sorrow is renewed for the family of Muḥammad in it."
He said: I said, "And why?" He said: "Because they see their right in the hands of others."

key_terms.آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the family of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.أَضْحًى: Eid al-Aḍḥā, the festival of sacrifice
key_terms.عِيدٍ: a festival day of communal religious celebration
key_terms.فِطْرٍ: Eid al-Fiṭr, the festival marking the end of sawm (fasting)

ai.seo_question: Why do Eid al-Aḍḥā and Eid al-Fiṭr renew sorrow for the family of Muhammad?
ai.summary: Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that the days of Eid renew sorrow for Āl Muḥammad because those occasions highlight that their rightful due remains with others. The hadith expresses the grief of the Ahl al-Bayt over usurped authority and rights despite the public celebration of the Muslim community.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2058 - It is narrated from Hanan ibn Sudair, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Abu Ja'far (as), who said:
"O Abdullah, there is no Eid for the Muslims, whether Eid al-Adha or Eid al-Fitr, except that it brings renewed sorrow to the family of Muhammad."

I asked: "Why is that?"
Imam (as) replied: "Because they see their right in the hands of others."
